blocks.text: Jesus had died on the cross on Friday. His friends laid his body in a tomb cut into the rock, and a great stone was rolled across the door. Then came the Sabbath, a day of rest and waiting. Sunday morning, before the sun was up, Mary went back.

verses.text: The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre.

blocks.text: The two of them ran the whole way. The other disciple got there first, and the gospel makes a point of saying so. It is easy to hear a little smile in that.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The first person to see Jesus risen was a woman standing by a grave in tears. He did not first appear to a crowd or to the leaders. He came to the one who stayed, and he called her by her name. Then he sent her to tell the others. She went, and her message was the oldest good news there is. I have seen the Lord.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to John 20:1-18; the Sabbath named only as the day between (no position on which day to keep); 'the other disciple' left unnamed as the text leaves him; Mary as first witness is the text.

cultural.note: Mary Magdalene shown as faithful and the first sent, never with the later legends about her past.
